title: Kernels, images, generated ideals and quotients of quasi-coherent algebras are quasi-coherent, computed on affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A *quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra* is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. (a) Let $\psi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebras. Then the kernel $\mathcal J=\ker\psi$ ($U\mapsto\ker\psi_U$) is a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$ which is quasi-coherent, the image $\operatorname{Im}\psi\subseteq\mathcal A$ (the subsheaf of local sections of $\mathcal A$ which are locally in the image of $\psi$) is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-algebra of $\mathcal A$ which is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U\subseteq X$: $\mathcal J(U)=\ker(\psi_U)$ and $(\operatorname{Im}\psi)(U)=\psi_U(\mathcal B(U))$. (b) Let $\mathcal B$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra, $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map. Let $(e(\mathcal E))\subseteq\mathcal B$ be the sheaf of ideals generated by $e(\mathcal E)$ (the smallest sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal B$ containing $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$ for all open $U$; it is the image of the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$, $b\otimes s\mapsto b\,e(s)$). Then $(e(\mathcal E))$ is quasi-coherent, and for every affine open $U$, $(e(\mathcal E))(U)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$ generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$. The quotient $\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))$ (sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal B(U)/(e(\mathcal E))(U)$) is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra with a surjective algebra map $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))$ such that for every affine open $U$ the map $q_U$ is surjective with kernel $(e(\mathcal E))(U)$, i.e. $(\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E)))(U)=\mathcal B(U)/(e(\mathcal E))(U)$; and for every morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\chi:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ with $\chi\circ e=0$ there is exactly one algebra map $\bar\chi:\mathcal B/(e(\mathcal E))\to\mathcal C$ with $\bar\chi\circ q=\chi$.

proof.text: The algebra map $\psi$ is linear by [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf]. Its module kernel is sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Each section kernel is an ideal since $\psi_U(cb)=\psi_U(c)\psi_U(b)=0$ when $\psi_U(b)=0$. This gives all the kernel assertions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-image] to $\psi$. Its local-image algebra has the underlying module image. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] this module is quasi-coherent and on every affine $U$ its sections are $\psi_U(\mathcal B(U))$. This proves the image assertions.

proof.text: For (b), [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-generated-ideal-tensor] constructs $\mu:\mathcal T=\mathcal B\otimes\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ and identifies its module image $\mathcal I$ with the generated ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections], $\mathcal T$ is quasi-coherent and $t_U$ is bijective on affine $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to $\mu$: $\mathcal I$ is quasi-coherent and $\mathcal I(U)=\mu_U\mathcal T(U)$. Via $t_U$, this image consists of finite sums $\sum b_j e_U(s_j)$, exactly the ideal generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$.

source.place: Tag 05JS, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, proof: B_i-ideal generated by F_{i,j}; general tensor/local-image construction via Sheaves Tag 0089, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-quotient-cokernel] to $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal B$: the ring-sheafified quotient $\mathcal Q$ has underlying module isomorphic to $\operatorname{Coker}(\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal B)$, intertwining the actual projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], this cokernel is quasi-coherent and on affine $U$ its projection is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I(U)$. The same holds for $q_U$ under the isomorphism, and $\mathcal Q(U)\cong\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal I(U)$ as algebras since $q_U$ is an algebra map. The quotient lemma also gives local surjectivity of $q$.

proof.text: If $\chi e=0$, the sectionwise kernels of $\chi$ form an ideal subsheaf containing $e(\mathcal E)$. Minimality in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-generated-ideal-tensor] implies $\chi\mathcal I=0$. The quotient universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-quotient-cokernel] now gives exactly the required unique algebra factorization.

lean.statement: theorem kernel_image_quasiCoherent {X : Scheme.{u}} (B A : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (hB : B.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (hA : A.toModule.IsQuasicoherent) (ψ : B ⟶ A) : (∃ (J : X.Modules) (i : J ⟶ B.toModule), J.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (i.app U) ∧ Set.range (i.app U) = (RingHom.ker (ψ.right.hom.app (op U)).hom : Set (B.right.obj.obj (op U)))) ∧ (∃ (D : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (k : D ⟶ A), D.toModule.IsQuasicoherent ∧ (∀ U : X.Opens, Function.Injective (k.right.hom.app (op U))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : A.right.obj.obj (op U)), s ∈ Set.range (k.right.hom.app (op U)) ↔ ∀ x : X, x ∈ U → ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U), x ∈ V ∧ A.right.obj.map (homOfLE hVU).op s ∈ Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op V))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → Set.range (k.right.hom.app (op U)) = Set.range (ψ.right.hom.app (op U))))
lean.note: Part (a) is kernel_image_quasiCoherent; part (b) is generated_ideal_quotient_quasiCoherent. Ideals are represented by module-sheaf inclusions with injective section maps and specified ideal ranges; no additional definition is introduced. Quotient presheaf sections are specified by surjectivity and kernel, and the quotient sheaf and its map are tied to the existing sheafification adjunction unit.
